newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK OTE AWARDS NEW CARDPHONE DEAL TO INTRAKOM.
newsitem.headline: GREEK OTE AWARDS NEW CARDPHONE DEAL TO INTRAKOM.

text.p: The board of directors of Greece's state telecoms OTE has decided to award a contract of 30,000 new technology cardphones to the Intrakom group, it said.
The OTE board of directors also decided against recommending the appointment of Nikos Tzaneteas to the post of its managing director, it said in the statement on Friday.
The appointment must be approved by the national economy and transportation ministers.
It said Tzaneteas was qualified for the job but he was not fluent in Greek and did not know much about the reality of the Greek market and business environment.

Tzaneteas was the first runner up in the short list of candidates to become its new managing director. The appointment of the first candidate was rejected by the government because he was not familiar with the telecommunications industry.
Intrakom and Siemens Hellas, a subsidiary of German Siemens AG, are OTE's main suppliers of digital switches.

Greek prosecutors have laid charges against unknown individuals for bribery and fraud in connection with a 1994 OTE procurement of about 1.0 million digital switches to Intrakom and Siemens. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
